title: Basis, dimension, and minimal spanning sets
terms: basis; minimal spanning set; dimension; finite-dimensional space; infinite-dimensional space; basis extension.

exposition.text:
A basis is a linearly independent spanning set. Every vector has a unique expression as a finite
linear combination of basis vectors. All bases of a finite-dimensional vector space have the same
size, its dimension. If no finite spanning set exists, the space is infinite dimensional.
In an n-dimensional space, any n independent vectors form a basis, and any n spanning vectors
form a basis. An independent list can be extended to a basis; a finite spanning list can be re-
duced to one. A proper subspace of a finite-dimensional space has smaller dimension. Counting
listed generators alone does not determine dimension until redundancy is removed.

question.text:
Six vectors span a four-dimensional real vector space. What is the least number that must be
removed to leave a basis, with suitable choices of vectors to remove?
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) 4

solution.text:
Every basis has exactly four vectors. The spanning-set reduction theorem guarantees a
four-element basis can be selected from the six, so exactly two are removed.

Every such polynomial is a finite linear combination of positive powers of x, and unique-
ness of polynomial coefficients proves their independence. No finite list suffices because
degrees are unbounded. A basis in an infinite-dimensional space still represents each vector
by a finite sum.

question.text:
Which assertion about a five-dimensional space is always true?
(A) Every list of four vectors is independent
(B) Every list of six vectors is dependent
(C) Every independent list spans
(D) Every spanning list has exactly five vectors
(E) Every list of five vectors is a basis

solution.text:
An independent list has at most the dimension many vectors. The other assertions omit in-
dependence, spanning, or cardinality requirements and admit elementary counterexamples.
